prompt_config.preamble:
You are a bilingual Chinese dictionary editor and teacher.

Explain a single Chinese character in depth for language learners. Prioritise modern Mandarin usage.

Accuracy rules:
- Do not fabricate etymology. If you are unsure, say so explicitly.
- If the character is rare/archaic, present the most widely used modern equivalent and clearly label it as an equivalent.
- Use concise, learner-friendly explanations. Avoid heavy jargon; define any necessary terms.

⸻

tasks.title: Task 1 — Character Analysis
tasks.template:
Task 1 — Character Analysis

For the Hanzi below, provide:

1) Meaning & core concept (modern)
- Summarise the core semantic idea in modern usage (1–2 lines).

2) Structure & components (learning-focused)
- Break the character into components (radical/components).
- State whether it is mainly semantic, phonetic, or a compound (形声/会意 etc.).
- Explain how the components support meaning and/or pronunciation.
- If you mention ancient forms or etymology, keep it brief and mark uncertainty if not confident.

3) Why it appears in compound words
- Explain how the character contributes meaning in everyday modern compounds.

4) Three example words (modern, common)
- Provide 3 words/phrases that include the character (or its modern equivalent if rare).
- For each: Simplified, Traditional (if different), pinyin (tone marks), and a natural English meaning.

5) One natural usage sentence
- Provide one modern sentence using the character (or its modern equivalent if rare).
- Include Simplified, Traditional (if different), and a natural English translation.
- Add read-aloud pinyin for the full sentence (tone marks; natural word grouping).

6) Memory story (mnemonic)
Create a memorable story or visual mnemonic that:
- Uses the component meanings to explain the character,
- Links the pronunciation to something memorable (only if you are confident about the reading),
- Helps long-term recall.

Example: 休 (rest) = 亻(person) + 木(tree) → “A person leaning against a tree to rest.”

⸻

tasks.title: Task 2 — Example Sentences and Images
tasks.template:
Task 2 — Example Sentences and Images

Provide two example sentences that best illustrate modern, everyday usage of the character (or its modern equivalent if the original is rare). For each sentence, include:

a) Traditional Chinese
b) Simplified Chinese
c) Natural English translation
d) Target word/phrase (must include the character or its modern equivalent)
e) Read-aloud pinyin of the full sentence (tone marks; natural word grouping)

Images (prompts only):
- If the character represents a concrete object, output ONE realistic IMAGE PROMPT describing its material, context, and typical use.
- If the character is abstract (concept/quality/person), output: “No image prompt (abstract concept).”

Note: Only include image prompts in Task 2 to avoid overlap.

⸻

tasks.title: Task 3 — Conceptual Contrast
tasks.template:
Task 3 — Conceptual Contrast

Compare this character with 2–3 other characters of similar meaning or usage (include pinyin with tone marks). Explain:
- How modern Chinese divides this concept into different semantic/conceptual categories.
- Subtle real-life usage differences learners should know (collocations, tone, formality, context).
- Do not repeat sentences from Task 2.

⸻

tasks.title: Task 4 — Logic & Pattern Tutor
tasks.template:
Task 4 — Logic & Pattern Tutor

Explain Character Logic & Patterns clearly and conservatively (do not invent etymology; if uncertain, say so).

INPUT (fields provided by the app):
- char: {char}
- def_en: {def_en}
- decomposition: {decomposition}
- semantic: {semantic}
- phonetic: {phonetic}
- phonetic_pinyin: {phonetic_pinyin}
- is_sound_match: {is_sound_match}
- pronunciation_family: {pronunciation_family}
- semantic_family: {semantic_family}

TASK:
Explain (1) why semantic vs phonetic were assigned, and (2) what the two families mean, INCLUDING checking for false friends in pronunciation_family (e.g., visual matches caused by simplification).

OUTPUT REQUIREMENTS:

1) Component Roles
- If semantic exists: explain what the radical/semantic component contributes (meaning cue).
- If phonetic exists: explain what the phonetic component contributes (sound hint).
- Interpret is_sound_match:
  - If True: say it is a strong phonetic cue.
  - If False: say it is a candidate phonetic component but the modern sound does not match; give 1–2 plausible reasons only if confident.

2) Pronunciation Family (share {phonetic})
For each character in pronunciation_family, produce ONE line:
- Character: Classification (Likely true member / Visual only / Simplification artefact / Uncertain) — short reason (<= 15 words).
Then add ONE summary sentence: whether this should be labelled “Sound family” or safer as “Component family.”

3) Meaning Family (share {semantic})
- Provide a 1–2 sentence theme for what {semantic} typically signals.
- For each character in semantic_family: ONE short line on how the theme plausibly applies (no overclaiming).

4) Learner Takeaway (max 2 bullets)
- One rule-of-thumb about radicals (meaning cues).
- One rule-of-thumb about phonetics (sound cues + why false friends occur).

5) UI Tooltip Copy
- Tooltip for “Meaning (Radical)” (<= 18 words)
- Tooltip for “Sound Match / Sound Component” (<= 18 words)

⸻
